cards.text: This is a psalm of David, king of Israel (2 Samuel 5:3), written for the choirmaster. Most work emails open with “Hope this finds you well.” David opens with “Rescue me, O LORD, from evil men.”

cards.question: David asks the LORD to protect him from men of violence. He says these men stir up ___ all day long.

cards.text: Then David gets to how these men talk, and whatever's on their lips is NOT sprinkles. Friend, it's poison.

cards.question: David says these violent men sharpen their tongues like ___.

cards.text: Then David asks again: “Guard me, O LORD, from the hands of the wicked.” Different words, same request, the man is following up on his own email.

cards.question: What does David say these men of violence are scheming to do to him?

cards.text: Now the picture changes: the proud are hiding something on David's path for him to walk right into. You ever step on a rake hidden in the leaves, except somebody put it there ON PURPOSE?

cards.question: What do the proud hide and spread along David's path?
With traps set along his path, David says to the LORD, “You are my God.”

cards.text: David calls Him O GOD the Lord, the strength of his salvation. Then the picture moves off the path with the traps and into the day of battle.

cards.question: In the day of battle, what does David say the LORD does for him?
Next David prays about the plans of the wicked. He asks the LORD to give them what they want.

cards.text: Now David prays about the heads of those who surround him. Two verses ago the LORD was shielding David's head, and friend, the only thing my chef's hat has EVER shielded me from is flour.

cards.question: David prays that the heads of those around him will be covered in the trouble their own ___ have caused.

cards.text: And David keeps going: “May burning coals fall on them; may they be thrown into the fire, into the miry pits, never to rise again.”

cards.question: David prays that no ___ will be established in the land, and that ___ will hunt down the man of violence.

cards.text: Then David's prayer changes gears. He stops asking and starts saying what he KNOWS about the LORD.

cards.question: What does David say he knows the LORD does for the poor?
David ends by saying the righteous will praise the LORD's name and the upright will dwell in His presence.

findings.problem: This poetry question asks the baker to complete the wording of David's line, "stir up ___ all day long." The opening card does not establish the men's all-day warmongering, so the baker cannot reason out "war" rather than "fear" or "doubt" from what has been told.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The blank asks the baker to supply the next words of David's simile, "sharpen their tongues like ___." This is wording completion of the psalm's line rather than a question about what the poisonous-speech picture means.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: This question asks for the unseen wording of verse 9, "the trouble their own ___ have caused." The immediately preceding story card sets up only the heads of David's enemies; it does not set up the connection between their speech and the trouble coming back on them.

findings.problem: Both blanks require the baker to guess the wording of verse 11. The preceding card quotes verse 10's burning coals, fire and pits, but gives no basis for reasoning out the new terms "slanderer" and "calamity," including the new picture of calamity hunting someone down.
